newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairie seeding 66 to 75 pct done - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairie seeding 66 to 75 pct done - CWB.

text.p: Spring seeding of Canada's six major grains and oilseeds was two-thirds to three-quarters completed by Monday, a Canadian Wheat Board analyst said.
"We're probably looking at getting close to three-quarters done but certainly easily more than two-thirds finished," CWB weather and crop analyst Bruce Burnett told Reuters.

All wheat seeded area on the Prairies was seen 9.2 percent down at 28.22 million acres in 1997 from 31.08 million acres the year before, Statistics Canada said April 30. Canola was seen up 32 percent to 11.585 million acres from 8.8 million.
"Seeding is general in all areas except for the flooded region," Burnett said.
About a half million acres of southern Manitoba's farmland were flooded when the Red River crested at its highest peak in 145 years earlier this month.
Manitoba and Saskatchewan had dry weather all weekend, while southern Alberta saw heavy rain Sunday into Monday, Environment Canada said.
Alberta's foothills saw 100 mm (4 inches) of rain, while Calgary and Lethbridge saw up to 70 mm (2.8 inches), Environment Canada meteorologist Francois Choquette said.
A weather warning remained in effect for Lethbridge, which was forecast to see up to 30 mm (1.2 inches) of rain on Monday.
"That's generally pretty good. They're finished seeding down there," the CWB's Burnett said.
That region was becoming dry until the weekend rains fell.
"Some of those areas in the foothills, if you have that much rain over a two-day period, that could cause some problems with washing out," Burnett said.
No regions reported killing frosts over the weekend, Environment Canada said.
There are 97 days from Monday to August 31.

Wheat needs 90 to 100 days to mature. Barley needs 60 to 90 days to mature, oats 85 to 88 days, flax 85 to 100 days, Argentine canola 92 to 102 days, Polish canola 73 to 83 days and field peas 90 to 100 days.
The average spring frost season for the Prairies ends between May 20 and 28, CWB weather and crop surveillance director Paul Bullock said.
Lows of -4.0 Celsius must last four hours to kill wheat, but spring crops can be reseeded and may reach maturity in time for fall harvest, Bullock said.
